questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is detergent called a soapless soap?
options: It has cleaning properties like soap but its chemical nature is different.
It does not give lather with hard water as soap.
It has the same chemical composition as soap.
It has cleaning properties like soap and can be used with hard water.
questions.explanation: Detergent cleans like soap. But chemically it is not soap, so it is called soapless soap.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Identify the group of insecticides.
questions.explanation: Dieldrin, DDT and methoxychloride are insecticides. They are used to kill insects.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In which group does sodium stearate lie?
questions.explanation: Sodium stearate is a salt of fatty acid. It is an example of soap.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main use of detergents?
questions.explanation: Detergents remove dirt from clothes. So their main use is washing clothes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which compound is used to ripen fruits?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide releases gas that helps fruits ripen. So it is used for artificial fruit ripening.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is soap chemically described as in the chapter?
options: Sodium or potassium salt of higher fatty acid
questions.explanation: Soap is a sodium or potassium salt of higher fatty acid. This is its chemical description.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which salt is an example of soap?
questions.explanation: Sodium stearate is a common soap. It is formed from stearic acid salt.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which chemical is used with fat or oil in soap making?
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide reacts with fat or oil. This reaction makes soap.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is common salt added during soap making?
questions.explanation: Common salt helps soap separate from the mixture. This step is called salting out.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is detergent mainly used for in daily life?
questions.explanation: Detergent is used to remove dirt and grease. So it is mainly used for washing clothes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which chemical is used for artificial ripening of fruits?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide is used for artificial fruit ripening. Misuse of it can be harmful.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which chemical is an insecticide?
questions.explanation: DDT is a chemical insecticide. It is used to control insects.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which chemical is also called benzene hexachloride?
questions.explanation: BHC means benzene hexachloride. So BHC is also called benzene hexachloride.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which term refers to chemicals that protect food from spoilage?
questions.explanation: Food preservatives slow down food spoilage. They help keep food usable for a longer time.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is a common natural food preservative?
questions.explanation: Salt removes water from microorganisms. So it helps preserve food naturally.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is another common natural food preservative?
questions.explanation: Sugar also reduces microbial growth in food. So it is a natural preservative.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which substance is used to preserve pickles?
questions.explanation: Pickles are preserved by salt, oil or vinegar. These materials reduce spoilage.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which daily-life chemicals can cause water pollution when used excessively?
questions.explanation: Too much soap and detergent can enter water. This pollutes water and harms aquatic life.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What kind of pesticide uses living organisms or natural enemies?
questions.explanation: Biological pesticides use living organisms or natural enemies. They control pests in a safer way.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is chemical pollution?
options: Pollution caused by harmful chemicals in the environment
questions.explanation: Chemical pollution is caused by harmful chemicals. These chemicals damage air, water or soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why should the use of DDT be controlled?
options: It is an ore of iron.
It is used to prepare ammonia.
questions.explanation: DDT can stay in the environment for a long time. It can harm living things and disturb the ecosystem.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why should chemical pesticides be decreased?
options: They can harm human health and the environment.
questions.explanation: Chemical pesticides can harm people, animals and soil. So their use should be reduced.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is salt used in soap making?
options: It helps separate soap from the mixture.
questions.explanation: Salt separates soap from the soap-making mixture. So soap can be collected easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why can pickles be preserved for a long time?
options: They are kept in lime water.
Preservatives such as salt, oil or acid reduce spoilage.
questions.explanation: Salt, oil or acid stops many microorganisms from growing. So pickles can last for a long time.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which full form of DDT is correct?
questions.explanation: DDT stands for dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane. This is its full chemical name.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which full form of BHC is correct?
questions.explanation: BHC stands for benzene hexachloride. This is its full form.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best compares soap and detergent?
options: Soap is an ore and detergent is a gas.
Both clean, but detergent has different chemical nature and works with hard water.
questions.explanation: Soap and detergent both clean dirt. Detergent is chemically different and works better in hard water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best compares chemical and biological pesticides?
options: Chemical pesticides are synthetic chemicals; biological pesticides use living agents or natural control.
questions.explanation: Chemical pesticides are man-made chemicals. Biological pesticides use living agents or natural control.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best compares chemical and organic food preservatives?
options: Chemical preservatives are added chemicals, while organic/natural preservatives come from natural materials.
questions.explanation: Chemical preservatives are added chemicals. Natural preservatives come from natural materials like salt or sugar.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which set contains only cleaning chemicals discussed in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Soap and detergent are cleaning chemicals. Both are used to wash and remove dirt.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which set contains only pesticides or insecticides from the chapter?
questions.explanation: DDT, dieldrin and methoxychloride are insecticides. They are used against insects.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main risk of excessive chemical pesticide use?
questions.explanation: Excess pesticides can enter food, soil and water. This causes health and environmental problems.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which alternative is suggested to reduce problems from chemical pesticides?
options: Use safer biological or organic methods
questions.explanation: Biological and organic methods are safer. They reduce harm from chemical pesticides.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which precaution should be taken while using chemical pesticides?
options: Use carefully and avoid direct contact or overuse
questions.explanation: Chemical pesticides can be poisonous. So they should be used carefully and not touched directly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is a natural method to preserve nutrients in food?
questions.explanation: Drying and proper storage reduce spoilage. They help preserve food without adding many chemicals.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which chemical used to ripen fruits can be harmful if misused?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide is used to ripen fruits artificially. If misused, it can be harmful to health.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which effect may result from detergents entering water bodies?
options: Water pollution and harm to aquatic life
questions.explanation: Detergents in water can pollute ponds and rivers. They can harm fish and other aquatic life.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which industrial products are mentioned as possible sources of chemical pollution?
options: Cement, glass, ceramics, plastic, fibre and fertilizers
questions.explanation: These industries can release harmful chemicals. Their wastes may pollute the environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which practical way helps minimize chemical pollution?
options: Reduce excessive chemical use and manage waste properly
questions.explanation: Using fewer chemicals reduces pollution. Proper waste management stops chemicals from spreading.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which food-preservation purpose is best described?
options: To collect CO2 in a jar
To prevent spoilage and keep food usable longer
questions.explanation: Food preservation prevents spoilage. It keeps food usable for a longer time.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A village has health and environmental problems due to excessive pesticide use. Which solution best follows the chapter?
options: Reduce chemical pesticides and use biological or safer alternatives
questions.explanation: Chemical pesticides should be reduced when they cause harm. Biological or safer methods protect health and environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A soap-making mixture contains fat/oil and sodium hydroxide. Which step helps separate soap from the mixture?
questions.explanation: Salt separates soap from the soap-making mixture. So adding salt helps collect soap.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A cleaning material works in hard water and is chemically different from soap. What is it?
questions.explanation: Detergent cleans in hard water. It is chemically different from soap.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which answer best explains why detergent is called soapless soap?
options: It cleans like soap but is not chemically soap.
questions.explanation: Detergent cleans like soap. But it is not chemically soap, so it is called soapless soap.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A farmer wants pest control with less environmental harm. Which choice is best according to the chapter idea?
options: Biological pesticide or reduced chemical use
questions.explanation: Biological pesticides cause less harm to the environment. Reduced chemical use also protects useful organisms.

questions.subject: science

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide is used for artificial fruit ripening. So this pair is correctly matched.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why can chemical pesticides create imbalance in an ecosystem?
options: They may kill useful organisms and persist in the environment.
questions.explanation: Chemical pesticides can kill useful organisms too. This can break the natural balance of an ecosystem.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the best argument for using natural preservatives when possible?
options: They are generally safer and reduce chemical load in food.
questions.explanation: Natural preservatives usually add less chemical load to food. So they are safer when used properly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which combined action best reduces chemical pollution from daily-life chemicals?
options: Use more pesticides and detergents together
Use chemicals carefully, prefer safer alternatives, and manage wastes properly
Dispose all wastes into water sources
Ripen all fruits with excess calcium carbide
questions.explanation: Careful use reduces harmful chemical release. Safer alternatives and proper waste management reduce pollution.
